messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated capacity SLO breach in us-west-2 for customer-facing inference pools. p95 ~ 4.2s (SLO 400ms), p99 ~ 12.4s (SLO 1s). Streaming stalls and partial response hangs reported. Queue depth jumped 10 -> ~620 across pool-22/23.

keon (oncall): saw the alert. looking at dashboards now. is this concentrated on streaming routes or batched requests too?

marta: streaming first, samir seeing some gen requests timing out as well (esp. long context). KV cache misses look high.

samir: stack: observed autoscaler not adding new reserved nodes for pool-22. Scale decision triggered but warmup jobs stuck waiting for handshake from runtime.

julia: customer impact: two large customers reported missing chunks in streaming. support ticket 98734 flagged degraded responses for 15+ min.

keon (oncall): marking priority P0 and paging infra-sre. @marta please start quick root-cause triage. Also enable on-call handoff ping.

marta: running logs:
```
2024-04-05T18:21:12Z autoscaler: decision:add 4 -> target_pending
2024-04-05T18:21:16Z runtime: pool-22 handshake timeout (waited 120s)
2024-04-05T18:22:02Z warmup: warmup task queued, but no free GPU slot; backoff retries
2024-04-05T18:22:34Z queue: depth=612, avg_wait=9.3s
```

marta: looks like compute handshake delays + NFS metadata lag caused warmups to stall. new instances allocated but never completed init.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated Pool Saturation -> steps: 1) assess root cause 2) throttle incoming burst 3) manual scale or route to fallback models 4) escalate to runtime if handshake. Link: https://runbook.internal/dedicated-saturation

keon (oncall): immediate mitigations we can try:
- enable queue-throttling policy for low-priority routes
- abort warmup timeout and try manual provisioning for 2 GPUs in pool-22
- temporarily route streaming -> hosted-fallback cluster for top-2 affected customers

samir: executing manual provisioning now: `infractl pool attach --pool pool-22 --gpus 2 --mode manual`

samir: seeing `attach` accepted but warmup stuck with `init: pulling kernel configs` on the new nodes. NFS reads are slow (high latency).

julia: support-liaison, recommend we send a short update to impacted customers: "we're investigating elevated latency and partial streaming interruptions; mitigation in progress, will follow up in 30m."

support-liaison: drafting message now. will include temporary workaround: ask app teams to fall back to non-streaming endpoints if possible.

marta: additional telemetry: KV cache cold miss rate increased 8x during the burst -> explains p99 blowups when model reloads occur. Also telemetry shows a spike in small keepalive connections causing scheduler pressure.

keon (oncall): manual mitigation results?

samir: manual provision completed for 2 nodes, but runtime handshake still failing for 90% of requests. I can force a restart of the runtime agent on those nodes: `ssh node-xy && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime` — will do after a quick thumbs from SRE.

marta: do it. restart should nudge handshake and clear warmup backlog.

samir: restarted runtime agent on node-xy and node-xz. warmup jobs resumed. queue depth dropped 620 -> 140 in ~60s. p95 back to ~550ms, p99 ~1.8s.

keon (oncall): good improvement. keep monitoring. keep throttling low-priority traffic for another 20m.

julia: live status update sent to customers. ticket 98734 updated with mitigation steps and ETA.

marta: root cause hypothesis: simultaneous customer bursts caused pool saturated; autoscaler calculated scale but warmup/handshake path failed due to transient NFS latency (metadata reads) combined with runtime agent sluggishness. Effectively autoscale decision pending but warmup couldn't finish -> sustained queue growth and streaming stalls.

keon (oncall): next actions:
- trust autoscaler for steady-state, but add a short-circuit for manual override if warmup fails X times in Y minutes
- add more aggressive retry/parallelism for runtime handshake during high queue pressure
- schedule follow-up postmortem with runtime and infra teams within 24h
- ops: consider pre-warming small buffer of hot nodes for top customers during predictable bursts

marta: filing incident record. I'll attach heap of logs and the timeline.

support-liaison: customers acknowledged update; one asked for credits — flagged for billing review.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). p95 under SLO for most traffic, p99 still elevated for a small tail. Postmortem required.

keon (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll remain on this thread for the handoff to the morning shift. @julia please start a concise summary for the doc (who/what/impact/mitigation/todo).

julia: on it, will post summary in incidents channel and link runbook + logs.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert resolved for now. Keep monitoring for 2 hours."
